passage: I'm Irawati, and last spring I asked a question I used to be too shy to ask. My adviser said, "Offer free delivery, always." The old me would have printed it on flyers that night. This time I asked, "Why?" She explained that in the big city people will not order without it, and the cost gets spread over many orders. That made sense for her city, but my town has one main road. So I asked Jahnavi, who runs a bakery in a town like mine. Jahnavi laughed. "Free delivery ate half my first month." I settled on free delivery only for the two nearest lanes, and a small charge beyond. Three months on, orders are steady and the numbers still make sense.

qa.q: What did Irawati ask the adviser?
What was Irawati thinking when she heard the adviser's reasons?
qa.a: Irawati realised the reasoning fitted the adviser's city but not a town with one main road, so she felt doubtful about using it as it was.

qa.q: What could Irawati do to check her final delivery rule?
qa.a: Irawati could track orders and delivery costs for a few weeks and change the lanes or the charge if the numbers do not fit.

qa.q: How might Jahnavi have felt when sharing that experience?
qa.a: Jahnavi may have felt glad to help and open about a costly lesson, since Jahnavi laughed and gave a plain answer.

grounding: Shows a person asking an adviser why, checking with another practitioner, and adapting the advice to her own customers.

Incubator mentor's note, week 6

Ira came to me after her session with Thomas, the pricing adviser. He had suggested she move her tutoring service to a monthly subscription. Instead of just nodding, she asked him why. He explained it worked for his clients because their families paid in advance. Ira then called a second practitioner, someone who runs a small tutoring centre locally, who said many parents here prefer paying per term, not per month. Ira brought both answers to me today. She has decided on a term plan with a small trial month for new families, a mix of both views fitted to her own parents. I suggested she ask ten current families before launching. She agreed and left with a question list.

qa.q: What did Thomas suggest to Ira?
qa.a: He suggested she move her tutoring service to a monthly subscription.

qa.q: What does Ira asking 'why' suggest about how she felt about the advice?
qa.a: She seems cautious and curious rather than doubtful; she wanted to feel sure the advice fitted her own families before acting.

qa.q: What else could Ira do before launching the term plan?
qa.a: Ask ten current families, as the mentor suggested, or run the trial month with a few families first and adjust.

qa.q: How might Thomas see Ira's decision to mix his idea with another?
qa.a: He might feel respected that she asked for his reasons, even if she didn't copy his plan exactly.

grounding: She asks the adviser for the reasoning, checks with a second practitioner and adapts the advice to her own customers.

Thursday night

Long day. At the market stall this morning I kept thinking about what the design adviser told me last week: "Switch all your pottery to matte glaze, it sells better." A week ago I would have just done it. Today I actually rang and asked why. Answer: in the city galleries, buyers want a modern look. Fair. But my buyers are tourists and local families who pick up mugs to use every day. So after lunch I called Payal, who has made pottery near the lake for years. She said matte shows tea stains faster, and her customers complain. Interesting! So here's my plan: matte for the decorative bowls, glossy for everyday mugs. I'll put six of each on the stall on Sunday and see what goes. Feeling clearer than I have all month. Manjula, you're learning.

qa.q: Who did Manjula call after lunch?
qa.a: Payal, who has made pottery near the lake for years.

qa.q: How is Manjula feeling at the end of the entry?
qa.a: Manjula feels clearer and more confident than all month, even a little proud: "Manjula, you're learning."

qa.q: Which other approach could Manjula use to test the plan?
qa.a: Ask a few regular buyers directly which finish they prefer, alongside the Sunday test with six of each.

qa.q: How might Payal see being asked for her view?
qa.a: Payal probably felt respected that her years of experience with local customers were valued.

grounding: The diarist asks an adviser why, checks with another practitioner and adapts the advice to Manjula's own customers.
